newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business press - Jan 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business press - Jan 6.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
THE TIMES
-- DIRECTORS NOT MEETING BOARDROOM PAY CODES OF PRACTICE

A survey has revealed that more than 400 executive directors of quoted companies either have no service contracts or fail to disclose the details of their contracts despite a legal requirement to do so. The survey carried out by Manifest, the proxy voting agency, has been submitted to the Hampel committee on corporate governance. It also shows serious divergence from the best practice in corporate governance laid down in the Cadbury and Greenbury codes.
-- INDUSTRY FACES SQUEEZE FROM STERLING RALLY

British industry faces a damaging year due to the sharp rise in sterling, according to the latest assessment of Britain's economic prospects from Oxford Economic Forecasting. As Britain acts to pre-empt inflation by raising interest rates, it will remove all the gains in British price competitiveness made since 1992. The report predicts the sterling's strength will prevent a runaway consumer boom this year but could create a slowdown in growth in 1998.
-- COVENTRY 30 MILLION STG TRANSFER TO QUOTED CLUBS TEAM

Coventry City, the Premiership team, plans to be the latest football club to join the stock market, with a 30 million stg flotation. Apax Partners has been appointed by the club to advise it on the float, planned for April.
THE GUARDIAN
-- VIRGIN SWEETENS WEST COAST LINE BID

Richard Branson's Virgin Group has pledged a 750 million stg investment in the West Coast Main Line rail franchise if it is successful in its bid to run the line. Virgin is already committed to a 250 million stg outlay for new rolling stock for CrossCountry rail, the rail franchise it takes control of today.
-- BAe SEEKS RULE CHANGE

British Aerospace and Rolls Royce have made presentations to Trade Secretary Ian Lang for a lifting of the restriction on foreign ownership of their shares. At present, 29.5 percent of shares in the two companies, both privatised in the 1980s, can be owned by foreign investors, but Rolls Royce says the limit impedes its possible stock market listing in the U.S. BAe believes the lifting of the restriction could help in the company's plans to play a leading role in the restructuring of the European aerospace and defence industry.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- BANKING BY TELEPHONE TO TAKE OFF BY 2001

According to new research, telephone banking is set to take off in Britain with some 30 percent of the population conducting their banking affairs by telephone by 2001. In a separate move, First Direct, Britain's phone-banking pioneer, is about to open a second call centre, to cope with its increased workload.
-- SCARDINO RECRUITED AS KEY PLAYER IN FOREST BID

Marjorie Scardino, who takes over as chief executive of Pearson this week has been recruited by a consortium that will make a last-minute bid for the Nottingham Forest football club. The consortium will present an offer document at noon on Monday to Forest chairman Irving Korn, which will be distributed to the club's 209 shareholders ahead of an extraordinary meeting to vote on a rival 13 million stg takeover proposal led by Porterbrook Leasing chief Sandy Anderson.
-- CLYDE ATTACKS 432 MILLION STG OFFER AS 'ON THE CHEAP'

Clyde Petroleum has attacked Gulf Canada's bid of 432 million stg as wholly inadequate. In a strongly worded defence document posted to shareholders yesterday, Clyde chairman Malcolm Gourlay said the offer totally failed to take account of the true value of Clyde and its continuing success.
